explain.say: Some things feel too big to say out loud, like being bullied, a friendship falling apart, or feeling low. The words get stuck! Look at the plan on the board. Step one: pick your person, someone you trust.

faq.q: When is a good time to talk about something hard?
faq.a: Choose a calm moment when the person is not busy or rushing, like after dinner, on a walk or in the car. You can also ask, "Can we talk later today?"
asks: When should I tell my parents?

faq.q: How do I start a difficult conversation?
faq.a: Use a simple starter line, like "Can I talk to you about something? It is hard to say." Then say what happened and how you feel, one small piece at a time.
asks: How do I tell someone something hard?

faq.q: What is an I feel sentence?
faq.a: It is a way to share feelings without blaming: "I feel... when... and I need..." For example, "I feel sad when I am left out, and I need help to fix it."

faq.q: What if I am too nervous to say it out loud?
faq.a: Write a note, send a message, or draw a picture. You can also bring a friend with you, or ask the grown-up to help by asking you questions.
asks: I am scared to talk about it

faq.a: Sometimes people are surprised at first and need a little time. If it is serious and they do not help, tell another trusted grown-up until someone does.
asks: What if my parents get angry?

facts: Psychologist Thomas Gordon made "I messages" popular in the 1970s as a way to talk about feelings without blaming others.
Many children's helplines let you chat by text or online if talking out loud feels too hard.

quiz.why: It shares your feeling and what caused it, without blaming.

wrong.1: This blames the other person, which can start an argument.
